key_insight: Helix4D adapts the expressive Trellis2 image-to-3D representation to video-conditioned 4D mesh generation by enabling cross-frame information sharing while preserving Trellis2's pretrained strengths, enabling robust reconstruction of complex topology, transparent materials, thin structures, and inner surfaces.
problem_solved: Existing video-to-4D methods fail on challenging phenomena (topology changes, transparency, thin geometry, inner surfaces) and lack temporally consistent dynamic meshes; Helix4D addresses these gaps to produce high-fidelity, time-consistent 4D meshes from video.
method: Extend Trellis2's frame-local attention with temporal cross-frame attention/aggregation so frames share information without degrading pretrained rare-case performance.

Produce a dynamic 4D mesh pipeline that updates topology and geometry over time (motion-aware mesh updates, handling birth/death of elements) to capture transparency, thin structures, and inner surfaces.

Train/finetune using a mix of pretrained weights and video supervision (temporal consistency losses and targeted augmentations) to retain expressiveness on rare cases while learning cross-frame coherence.
impact: Helix4D enables practitioners to convert video into temporally coherent, high-detail dynamic meshes that handle previously intractable visuals—useful for animation, AR/VR, simulation, and digital content creation workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side before/after: frames reconstructed with prior video-to-4D vs Helix4D highlighting thin structures and transparency improvements.
Model schematic: Trellis2 block (frame-local attention) augmented with cross-frame attention paths and dynamic mesh update module.
Timeline / 4D sequence: a short strip showing mesh evolution across time, emphasizing topology changes and inner-surface capture.
Close-up comparisons: zoomed renderings of transparent/ thin regions and inner surfaces with per-vertex error/consistency overlays.
paper_authors: Jiraphon Yenphraphai, Jianqi Chen, Jian Wang, Gordon Qian, Sergey Tulyakov
